videos.title: Neighbourhood INSIGHTS: What can the NHS learn from neighbourhood working in other policy areas?
videos.description:
Join the Strategy Unit for the next session in the Neighbourhood INSIGHTS series, exploring how evidence and analysis can support the shift from hospital to community.

The NHS is developing its approach to neighbourhood working. Together with partners in other services and sectors, it is devising new ways of working, and new ways of relating with local communities.

There is much to learn from practice elsewhere. And there is a long, rich tradition of neighbourhood working in other policy areas. Programmes such as Big Local, New Deal for Communities and Pride in Place; initiatives such as the Independent Commission on Neighbourhoods, and organisations like Local Trust. All act as potential sources of insight.   

In this session, James Plunkett, Kinship Works and author of End State, will reflect upon this practice, drawing out potential lessons for neighbourhood health. In doing so, he will also address the tricky and perennial question of ‘scaling up’ good practice.

videos.title: The risks of risk stratification in neighbourhood health
videos.description:
Neighbourhoods INSIGHTS' Series -The risks of risk stratification in neighbourhood health

The theory behind risk stratification is seductive. Almost irresistible in fact. It is that running algorithms over (mainly) primary care data will allow services to spot individual patients at high risk of unplanned hospital care. And then – by intervening early – that services can prevent poor outcomes. 
This has not worked in practice. Indeed, the reverse may be closer to the truth: evidence suggests that this use of risk stratification may even increase the use of unplanned care. 
So what has gone wrong? Where does this leave us? And what does this evidence mean for people planning and delivering neighbourhood health? 
This session, chaired by Fraser Battye, will present insights from Steven Wyatt (Strategy Unit), Jess Morley (Yale University) and Thea Stein (Nuffield Trust).

videos.title: SU Insights   Downsides of Digital
videos.description:
This event in collaboration with the Health Foundation featuring Professor Trish Greenhalgh and experts explored the critical questions on the downsides of digital, drawing on research to reflect the implications of digital technology in health and care.
 
There is widespread enthusiasm for the use of digital technology in health and care services, and shifting ‘from analogue to digital’ is one of the government’s priorities for the NHS. This shift promises significant gains in efficiency and productivity, and there are growing examples showing its potential in practice.
But are we aware of the trade-offs that come with these advancements? Do we know what losses may accompany promised gains? Are there looming risks and downsides that need more attention? And what do we know already from the implementation of digital technologies? What lessons can be learnt?
Event highlights include:
Fresh perspectives on the risks of using digital technology in health and care.
Insights into where digital technology can be helpful or harmful in health care.
An overview of our recently published discussion document on the downsides of digital
Presentations and discussions on the latest research, evidence and analysis.
Key speakers:
Fraser Battye, Head of Policy, Strategy Unit
Trish Greenhalgh, Professor of Primary Care Health Sciences, University of Oxford
Ellen Coughlan, Improvement Fellow, Health Foundation
Ben Shemesh, Senior Improvement Analyst, Health Foundation
Mahmoda Begum (Chair), Strategic Communications Lead, Strategy Unit

videos.title: SU Insights - Contracting for Health Outcomes
videos.description:
The inaugural ‘SU Insights’ session explore the evolving landscape of "Contracting for health outcomes". 
 
The concept of outcomes-based commissioning was a hot topic in health policy around 15 years ago. Innovative contracting models were promoted as a way to transform the way services were paid for, to unleash innovation in delivery. But the reality fell short of expectations. Few schemes made it past the design stage. Of the few that did, many failed - often expensively.

In this panel discussion leading experts explored the challenges and potential of outcomes-based commissioning in healthcare, why past efforts fell short, and what technical developments might help make these models more feasible today. 

Presented by the Strategy Unit, in collaboration with the Centre for Health Economics University of York, The Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS FT, NHS Confederation, and NHS England. 

Sign up here to be the first to hear about our next event: https://www.smartsurvey.co.uk/s/Strategy_Unit_Updates/

videos.title: Is ‘Do With’ the essence of neighbourhood health?
videos.description:
Event 3: Is ‘Do With’ the essence of neighbourhood health?

Neighbourhood health is often discussed in terms of services: how they are structured, funded and delivered.

But at its heart, it is about something more fundamental - relationships.

In particular, the relationships between services and the people they support.

A growing movement has emerged around this idea. Often described as ‘Do With’, it challenges traditional models of care that are designed ‘for’ people, or done ‘to’ people - instead advocating for approaches that are built with them.

Is this the essence of neighbourhood health?

If so, why does it matter? And what does it take to build and sustain more meaningful, community-centred relationships?

This session explores:
• What is meant by ‘Do With’ - and where this movement comes from
• Why relationships are central to neighbourhood health
• And how can richer service-citizen relationships be created and sustained?

The session, chaired by Fraser Battye, will present insights from Dr Connie Junghans Minton (Imperial College London) and Adam Lent (Kings Fund). It will examine the intangible and important question of how services ‘Do With’, rather than, ‘Do To’ people.

videos.title: NNHIP Evaluation and Analysis CoP: Drop in Sesssion NNHIP Care Shift Tracker
videos.description:
NNHIP Evaluation and Analysis CoP: Drop in Sesssion NNHIP Care Shift Tracker - 04.03.26

In this Evaluation and Analysis Community of Practice drop-in session, there was and demo of a tool that is being developed to offer a system-wide view using a range of indicators to help spot emerging patterns, enablers and blockers relating to shifting care. 

The NNHIP Care Shift Tracker
The challenge: Health and care systems, localities and communities are taking action to shift care away from hospitals where appropriate. Many of these actions are focussed on admissions avoidance, but in a complex and interdependent system, this alone will not be sufficient to shift care. Other activities and resource must also shift.

What this tool offers: The Care Shift Tracker app offers a system-wide view of relevant indicators. Because no single metric can tell us whether care is shifting, this tool brings together indicators across acute, community, workforce and spend to help you spot emerging patterns - and understand what might be enabling or blocking progress.

Helps to answers the questions:Is care shifting from hospital to other settings? What are the blockers and enablers?

About the CoP
The Evaluation and Analysis Community of Practice (CoP) is part of the NNHIP Intelligence Centre. videos.description:
The National Neighbourhood Health Implementation Programme (NNHIP) Evaluation and Analysis Community of Practice (CoP), has been set up as part of the NNHIP Intelligence Centre.
 
This CoP has been created directly in response to feedback that it would be helpful to have a dedicated space for local coaches, analysts, and others with analysis or evaluation as part of their role to come together, share learning, and learn from one another.

We run fortnightly, online drop-in sessions. These provide:
• a space for us to share relevant tools, products and updates from the Intelligence Centre;
• an opportunity for you to ask questions and discuss challenges you’re facing locally; and
• a way for you to shape future sessions by suggesting topics that would be most useful.

We record the first part of the session and this is followed by an open Q&A.

This session (21/1/26) focussed on the Neighbourhood Index which is currently being rolled out: 
https://neighbourhood-health.co.uk/news/the-neighbourhood-health-index

We are asking GP practices to display a poster (available in 14 languages) which tells patients about the survey.  


We're very much looking forward to building this community with you. If you have any questions about this CoP, please email me (Rachel.caswell@nhs.net)
